title: Debounce lid-close suspend so a quick reopen does not sleep in the dark
author: ijt
body:
Fixes https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/12193

## Why

logind's default `HandleLidSwitch=suspend` and Hyprland's lid bind both fire on the same close. A 2-second close/open then commits to S3 with the lid already open. `user.slice` is frozen, so Hyprland never sees `switch:off` and the panel stays at the lid-closed backlight. On this machine that looked like a hang and needed a power-button hold.

## What

- Packaged logind drop-in: `HandleLidSwitch=ignore` (and ExternalPower). Docked stays ignore.
- `omarchy-system-lid-close` still locks immediately, then starts `omarchy-system-lid-suspend`.
- That helper waits 3s (override `OMARCHY_LID_SUSPEND_DELAY`), then `systemctl suspend` only if the lid is still shut, there is no external monitor, and suspend is not toggled off.
- Lid open (`omarchy-system-lid-open`) cancels the pending job, runs `omarchy-system-wake`, and forces DPMS on. `omarchy-brightness-display on` can no-op when `dpmsStatus` is already true after S3 with backlight saved at 0.
- systemd-sleep `post` hook wakes the session 1s after thaw, because the compositor missed the lid event while frozen.
- Migration reloads logind once the drop-in is on disk.

## Not in this PR

The 20s delay used locally on a MacBookPro14,2. That number is because Alpine Ridge S3 resume is ~7s on that hardware (see the sibling Alpine Ridge PR). The portable debounce is 3s.

## Test plan

- Undocked: close lid 2s, open. Session locks, does not suspend, panel comes back.
- Undocked: close lid, leave closed. Suspends after ~3s.
- Docked: lid close stays awake on the external display.
- `omarchy toggle suspend` off: lid close locks, does not suspend.
- `./test/cli` and the lid-* / monitor-recovery shell tests.

Proven on Omarchy 4.0.2-1, MacBookPro14,2, kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2.
